newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks sprint home to end at highs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks sprint home to end at highs.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2267 +39 US 30yr cl 6.99 -0.03
*Stocks end at day's highs as stronger metals prices and a bond rally lures buyers into the market. Turnover 240.67 million shares, A$666.85 million value, 965 traded, 295 steady, 406 up, 264 down.

The Australian share market sprinted home to end at its day's high on Wednesday as buyers re-emerged after metal prices firmed overseas and bonds rallied as the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged.
At 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 24.1 points higher at 2252.8.
The September share price index was 39 points up at 2267 and at a 14.2 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said local investors had taken heart from interest rate developments in the U.S. and gold and base metals prices that showed signs of a rebound, at least in the short term.
"You have seen renewed interest in the metals stocks on the back of firmer copper and gold prices," said dealer Martin Angel of Perth-based broker Eyres Reed.
"The selldown was overdone and after yesterday's meeting, some investors are back on BHP's side."
Angel noted the unchanged U.S. interest rate scenario, saying while it may give mixed signals to U.S. investors, local players seemed to be happy with the Australian implications.
"I'm not sure whether leaving rates unchanged was a good or bad thing, but certainly some people locally are more comfortable that we may come down a touch," he said.
Major mining stocks CRA and BHP led the way in the resources sector, showing strength right from the start after some share price hammerings recently.
In the industrials, the big banks soared as the bond market rallied.

Commonwealth Bank instalment receipts again took the leading role, climbing more than three percent, but a solid supporting performance came from ANZ Bank which touched a record high of A$7.05 before closing at A$7.04.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bond yields closed at their lowest level in a month as the market rallied strongly in response to an unchanged U.S. rates which fuelled hopes of another local easing. However, profit-taking set in after the December 10-year bond futures contract just fell short of taking out August's 92.210 peak. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), 10-year T-bonds were yielding 7.86 percent, down 0.06 from Tuesday.

The Australian dollar ground to a softer finish as stubborn U.S. selling failed to be mopped up by Asian demand. But the currency did glean some support from the U.S. rates decision. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the currency was quoted at US$0.7880/85.
